facts.claim: Open GitHub issue #58 (live, confirmed) explains the mechanism's origin: the Claude Code Workflow tool's only code-sharing primitive is `workflow('name', args)`, capped at one nesting level — a child workflow calling `workflow()` throws 'workflow() cannot be called from within a child workflow.' The 4 shared modules used to be separate scripts invoked via `workflow('name')` from each stage script (itself already a child workflow of the orchestrator), which hit that cap; inlining them as copied blocks frees the one nesting level for a case that needs it. This also explains why 7 of the 9 scripts end in a top-level `return` — the Workflow tool executes each script's source as an AsyncFunction body, not a standard module.
